text:
alex: heads-up — noticed sustained RSS growth on a 2h streaming-chat + tool-loop run. pattern looks like KV slot residency increasing gradually, not single big jump. :thinking:

maria: hmm, which workload? repro script or customer trace?

alex: internal stress harness (50 concurrent sessions calling tools every ~30s). attached quick profile: resident +620MB over 90m. no obvious OOM, just steady climb.

rahul: can you paste the debug /kv stats output? curious about eviction_rate / pinned_pages.

alex: here are the relevant bits from /debug/kv/stats (trimmed):
```
total_slots: 1_024_000
active_slots: 812_300
evicted_pages: 12_380
eviction_rate_per_min: 1.5
pin_count_highwater: 5
fragmentation_ratio: 1.18
kv_reuse_hits: 42%
prefix_cache_hits: 9%
```

ingrid: fragmentation_ratio >1.1 over long runs is suspicious — could be small-slab pinning. Did jemalloc show many small arenas?

alex: ran jemalloc stats dump, saw lots of 256B allocations surviving; suspect per-request ephemeral structs pinned in the KV page table during streaming tool callbacks.

perf-bot: [metric-alert] kv_residency_growth_high on test-run-2026-03-12 — slope > 5MB/min for 90min :warning:

maria: any recent kernel selection / batching changes that touch slot layout or GC timing? we rolled the batching heuristic tweak last week (reduce max-batch-time from 8ms -> 3ms).

rahul: batching shouldn't change residency unless it altered key lifetime semantics (e.g., more concurrent inflight requests keep more prefixes live). Also changed KV compaction schedule?

alex: compaction config unchanged. hypothesis: faster batches increased concurrency of tool-call KV writes, leaving more partial page references alive until flush, causing micro-fragmentation and preventing page reuse.

ingrid: can we repro with a deterministic script that simulates tool loop order and concurrent batching? if yes, we can run with KV instrumentation enabled (slot-age histogram + page-refcounts).

alex: yes — I have a minimal repro: curl stream that opens a chat, then issues 1k tool calls chained. command:
```bash
for i in {1..10}; do \
  curl -N -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/stream -d @payload_$i.json &
done
wait
```
payloads chain tools with short delays. running with --kv-instrumentation on prints per-slot last-touch, refcount.

maria: run with --kv-defrag-run=1 after 30m and compare RSS delta. if defrag brings RSS down, fragmentation is likely.

rahul: also collect /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup and page_fault stats to see anon vs mapped growth.

alex: did a quick run: defrag triggered at t+35m reduced RSS by ~180MB, but growth resumed after ~20m. suggests defrag helps but leak/residency still accumulating.

ingrid: that points to slow leak of slots (not permanent because defrag reclaims some), maybe pinned by in-flight tool callbacks not releasing references promptly. do we have stack traces when slot refcounts >1 for long time?

alex: enabling slow-ref logging — will dump stacks for refs > 30s. attaching sample:
```
[2026-03-12T10:22:34] slot=0x7f8a2a id=12345 refs=2 last_touch=1900s
  stack: runtime::handle_tool_callback -> runtime::finish_stream -> kv::touch_slot
```

maria: ah — runtime::handle_tool_callback holds a scoped reference until callback completion, but we changed callback scheduling to defer completion ack until post-commit (for batching). that could extend ref lifetimes.

rahul: revert the post-commit ack optimization on the tool path as an experiment. if growth stops, we've got a causal link.

alex: running revert branch on a 2h run now, will report.

perf-bot: [deploy] revert/tool-ack-shim deployed to canary 3 instances at 2026-03-12T11:05Z :rocket:

maria: good. also add a test with forced rapid churn (many short-lived sessions) to ensure no regression for throughput.

alex: preliminary canary looks promising — slope dropped to ~0.2MB/min. I'll keep it running for another 2h. if green we'll ship small rollback and then plan a safer redesign (release scoped refs earlier + explicit transfer to async queue).

ingrid: also add a KV metric for "avg_ref_lifetime" to the console so future changes show up sooner.

alex: agreed. filing a follow-up perf ticket with repro steps, logs, and suggested fix. assigning to @maria for rollout plan. :+1:

maria: ack. thanks all.

(threads like this are short — I'll paste the run artifacts to the ticket when done.)
